7	---
8	
9	## Purpose
10	
11	This file documents `comments` (declared in `src/server/db/schema/comments.ts`) and
12	`attachments` (declared in `src/server/db/schema/issues.ts`, alongside `issues`, `labels` and
13	`issue_labels` — its schema-file placement does not match this dictionary's file split, and
14	this dictionary follows the assigned documentation split rather than the schema file
15	boundary). Both tables hang off `issues`: every comment and every attachment names an
16	`issue_id`, and neither table has any existence independent of an issue.
17	
18	## `comments`
19	
20	**Drizzle export:** `comments` in `src/server/db/schema/comments.ts`
21	**Soft delete:** yes (`archived_at`)
22	**Tenant column:** `org_id`
23	
24	| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
25	|---|---|---|---|---|
26	| `id` | TEXT | no (PK) | — | ULID, typed `CommentId` |
27	| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | denormalized alongside `issue_id`, per ADR-006 |
28	| `issue_id` | TEXT | no | — | typed `IssueId`; REQ-090 |
29	| `author_id` | TEXT | no | — | typed `UserId` |
30	| `body` | TEXT | no | — | restricted Markdown subset, REQ-091 |
31	| `parent_id` | TEXT | yes | — | typed `CommentId`; builds reply threads within one issue |
32	| `edited_at` | TEXT | yes | — | null until the author edits; REQ-097/REQ-102 |
33	| `mentioned_user_ids` | TEXT | no | `'[]'` | JSON array of `UserId`, "kept denormalised for the mention fan-out" per the schema file's own comment |
34	| `created_at` | TEXT | no | now | |
35	| `updated_at` | TEXT | no | now | |
36	| `archived_at` | TEXT | yes | — | REQ-098, deletion is a soft delete |
37	
38	**Indexes**
39	
40	| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
41	|---|---|---|---|
42	| `comments_org_issue_idx` | `org_id, issue_id` | no | the thread-loading query, `listThread`/`listComments` |
43	| `comments_org_archived_idx` | `org_id, archived_at` | no | default listings excluding archived comments, REQ-101 |
44	
45	**Invariants**
46	
47	- **A comment is never physically removed even after archiving (REQ-098), specifically
48	  because removing it would orphan any reply still pointing at it via `parent_id`** — this is
49	  the one piece of schema-design reasoning stated directly in `repository-issue-and-comment.md`
50	  (DES-186) and repeated here because it is the clearest justification in the whole
51	  corpus for why a *specific* table needs soft delete rather than hard delete: the `parent_id`
52	  self-reference makes hard deletion structurally unsafe, not merely undesirable.
53	- **`mentioned_user_ids` is denormalized JSON, not a join table**, unlike `issue_labels`'s
54	  normalized many-to-many shape for issue/label associations. The schema file's own comment
55	  explains why: it exists specifically "for the mention fan-out" — reading which users were
56	  mentioned in a comment to generate notifications (REQ-095) is a single-row read against this
57	  column, not a join, because that read happens on the comment-creation hot path.
58	- **Mentions are parsed at write time, not read time (REQ-092)**, and mentions inside code
59	  spans/fences are excluded (REQ-093) — both are `src/lib/mentions.ts` parsing rules applied
60	  before `insertComment` writes `mentioned_user_ids`, not something this column's shape alone
61	  enforces; a caller that bypassed the parser could write an arbitrary JSON array here.
62	- **Editing a comment re-parses its mentions (REQ-102)** — `updateComment`'s effect on
63	  `mentioned_user_ids` is not a passthrough of the caller's input; the mention set is
64	  recomputed from the new `body` the same way it was on creation, keeping the denormalized
65	  column consistent with the text it describes.
66	- **Mentioned users must already be members of the organization (REQ-094)** — enforced by
67	  `CommentService` cross-checking parsed mentions against `members` before persisting, not by
68	  any constraint this table's columns express.
69	- **Comment creation is rate limited per organization (REQ-096)** — via `rate_limit_buckets`
70	  (`tables-webhooks-search-and-infra.md`), a table entirely separate from `comments` itself;
71	  the rate limit is checked before `insertComment` runs, not enforced by anything in this
72	  table's own shape.
73	
74	**Read and write paths**
75	
76	`src/server/repositories/comment-repository.ts`: `findCommentById`, `listComments` (keyset-
77	paginated, archive-filtered by default per REQ-101), `listThread` (full thread for one issue,
78	un-paginated, archived comments included — REQ-100's creation-time ordering applies here),
79	`countComments`, `insertComment`, `updateComment`, `archiveComment`. `CommentService` is the
80	sole caller, and it is also the layer that calls `src/lib/mentions.ts` and
81	`src/lib/markdown.ts` (REQ-091's restricted subset) before any write.
82	
83	**Notes**
84	
85	The contrast between `listComments` (paginated, filtered) and `listThread` (full, unfiltered)
86	is deliberate and worth understanding as a pair: a comment *list* view (say, a recent-activity
87	feed spanning many issues) needs pagination and normally shouldn't show archived comments, but
88	a single issue's comment *thread* view needs every comment including archived ones, because
89	REQ-100's creation-time ordering and the reply-chain structure via `parent_id` both depend on
90	the full, unbroken sequence being visible — a thread with a silently-missing archived comment
91	in the middle would break the visual thread structure a reader expects, even if that comment's
92	own content is hidden or shown as "deleted."
93	
94	## `attachments`
95	
96	**Drizzle export:** `attachments` in `src/server/db/schema/issues.ts`
97	**Soft delete:** no — hard deleted; the schema file's own comment calls this out explicitly:
98	"there is no soft-delete story for bytes that no longer exist"
99	**Tenant column:** `org_id`
100	
101	| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
102	|---|---|---|---|---|
103	| `id` | TEXT | no (PK) | — | ULID, typed `AttachmentId` |
104	| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | denormalized alongside `issue_id`, per ADR-006 |
105	| `issue_id` | TEXT | no | — | typed `IssueId` |
106	| `filename` | TEXT | no | — | original filename |
107	| `content_type` | TEXT | no | — | MIME type |
108	| `size_bytes` | INTEGER | no | — | feeds the storage quota, REQ-075 |
109	| `uploaded_by` | TEXT | no | — | typed `UserId` |
110	| `created_at` | TEXT | no | now | |
111	| `updated_at` | TEXT | no | now | |
112	
113	**Indexes**
114	
115	| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
116	|---|---|---|---|
117	| `attachments_org_issue_idx` | `org_id, issue_id` | no | the per-issue attachment list, `listAttachments` |
118	
119	**Invariants**
120	
121	- **Hard delete, uniquely among tenant-scoped content tables in this schema.** `deleteAttachment`
122	  physically removes the row. This table stores metadata about the attachment (filename,
123	  content type, size), not the bytes themselves — the bytes' actual storage location is outside
124	  this schema's scope, and a hard-deleted row is consistent with there being no soft-delete
125	  story for content that has genuinely been removed from wherever the bytes live.
126	- **Attachment storage counts against the org's `storageMb` quota (REQ-075), a quota separate
127	  from `issuesPerProject` or `seats`.** `sumStorageBytes(orgId)` sums `size_bytes` across every

129	  "not yet hard-deleted," and the sum is exact rather than an archived-vs-live distinction.
130	- No column here records anything about virus scanning, content validation, or storage
131	  location — this table is purely metadata bookkeeping plus a size figure for quota purposes;
132	  any such concerns belong to whatever service actually persists the bytes, which is outside
133	  the scope of this schema.
134	
135	**Read and write paths**
136	
137	`src/server/repositories/attachment-repository.ts`: `listAttachments`, `insertAttachment`,
138	`deleteAttachment`, `sumStorageBytes`. `AttachmentService` and `IssueService` are the callers —
139	`AttachmentService` is the write path (upload and delete), and `sumStorageBytes` specifically
140	feeds `BillingService`'s quota checks, per this table's own repository file comment noting it
141	"feeds `storageMb` quota via `BillingService`."

147	it is easy to assume every content table in this schema follows the same archive-not-delete

| `edited_at` | TEXT | yes | — | null until the author edits; REQ-097/REQ-102 |

| `updated_at` | TEXT | no | now | |

  corpus for why a *specific* table needs soft delete rather than hard delete: the `parent_id`
  self-reference makes hard deletion structurally unsafe, not merely undesirable.
- **`mentioned_user_ids` is denormalized JSON, not a join table**, unlike `issue_labels`'s
  normalized many-to-many shape for issue/label associations. The schema file's own comment
  explains why: it exists specifically "for the mention fan-out" — reading which users were
  mentioned in a comment to generate notifications (REQ-095) is a single-row read against this
  column, not a join, because that read happens on the comment-creation hot path.

  recomputed from the new `body` the same way it was on creation, keeping the denormalized
  column consistent with the text it describes.

  `CommentService` cross-checking parsed mentions against `members` before persisting, not by
  any constraint this table's columns express.
- **Comment creation is rate limited per organization (REQ-096)** — via `rate_limit_buckets`
  (`tables-webhooks-search-and-infra.md`), a table entirely separate from `comments` itself;
  the rate limit is checked before `insertComment` runs, not enforced by anything in this
  table's own shape.

**Read and write paths**

paginated, archive-filtered by default per REQ-101), `listThread` (full thread for one issue,

`countComments`, `insertComment`, `updateComment`, `archiveComment`. `CommentService` is the

REQ-100's creation-time ordering and the reply-chain structure via `parent_id` both depend on
the full, unbroken sequence being visible — a thread with a silently-missing archived comment
in the middle would break the visual thread structure a reader expects, even if that comment's
own content is hidden or shown as "deleted."

## `attachments`

**Drizzle export:** `attachments` in `src/server/db/schema/issues.ts`
**Soft delete:** no — hard deleted; the schema file's own comment calls this out explicitly:
"there is no soft-delete story for bytes that no longer exist"

| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | denormalized alongside `issue_id`, per ADR-006 |
| `issue_id` | TEXT | no | — | typed `IssueId` |

| `size_bytes` | INTEGER | no | — | feeds the storage quota, REQ-075 |
| `uploaded_by` | TEXT | no | — | typed `UserId` |
| `created_at` | TEXT | no | now | |
| `updated_at` | TEXT | no | now | |

**Indexes**

| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attachments_org_issue_idx` | `org_id, issue_id` | no | the per-issue attachment list, `listAttachments` |

**Invariants**

- **Hard delete, uniquely among tenant-scoped content tables in this schema.** `deleteAttachment`
  physically removes the row. This table stores metadata about the attachment (filename,
  content type, size), not the bytes themselves — the bytes' actual storage location is outside
  this schema's scope, and a hard-deleted row is consistent with there being no soft-delete

**Read and write paths**

`src/server/repositories/attachment-repository.ts`: `listAttachments`, `insertAttachment`,
`deleteAttachment`, `sumStorageBytes`. `AttachmentService` and `IssueService` are the callers —
`AttachmentService` is the write path (upload and delete), and `sumStorageBytes` specifically
feeds `BillingService`'s quota checks, per this table's own repository file comment noting it
"feeds `storageMb` quota via `BillingService`."

**Notes**

`attachments` is the schema's clearest example of a table where the ADR-004 soft-delete
default was deliberately *not* applied, and the reasoning is worth restating precisely because
it is easy to assume every content table in this schema follows the same archive-not-delete
pattern: soft delete exists to preserve recoverability and audit-trail resolvability for rows

1	---
2	title: Billing and plan limits
3	status: approved
4	owners: [platform-team]
5	last_updated: 2026-06-20
6	related: [REQ-130, REQ-131, REQ-132, REQ-133, REQ-134, REQ-135, REQ-136, REQ-137, REQ-138, REQ-141, REQ-142, REQ-143, REQ-144, ADR-006, ADR-010, DES-209, DES-136]
7	---
8	
9	## Purpose
10	
11	This file documents `subscriptions` and `invoices`, declared together in
12	`src/server/db/schema/billing.ts`. Both tables are the persisted half of Taskflow's plan and
13	quota system, whose declarative half is `PLAN_LIMITS` in `src/config/plan-limits.ts` —
14	**ADR-010**, "Declare every plan quota in one table" (as implemented, that "table" is a single
15	in-code constant object, not a SQL table; see the note at the end of this file)
16	is the design record for why quotas are declared once and read everywhere rather than stored
17	per-organization. `organization_usage`, the table that measures *consumption* against these
18	quotas, is documented in `tables-organizations-and-users.md` since it is declared in
19	`organizations.ts`, not `billing.ts` — this file is about the *entitlement* side (what plan an
20	org is on, what it is billed) rather than the *consumption* side.
21	
22	## `subscriptions`
23	
24	**Drizzle export:** `subscriptions` in `src/server/db/schema/billing.ts`
25	**Soft delete:** no — a subscription's lifecycle is its own `status` enum, not archiving
26	**Tenant column:** `org_id`
27	
28	| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
29	|---|---|---|---|---|
30	| `id` | TEXT | no (PK) | — | ULID, typed `SubscriptionId` |
31	| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | REQ-130, exactly one subscription per organization |
32	| `plan` | TEXT | no | `'free'` | enum: `free`, `starter`, `growth`, `enterprise` — the same four-value ladder as `organizations.plan` (REQ-131) |
33	| `interval` | TEXT | no | `'monthly'` | enum: `monthly`, `annual` |
34	| `status` | TEXT | no | `'trialing'` | enum: `trialing`, `active`, `past_due`, `canceled` |
35	| `seats` | INTEGER | no | `1` | contracted seat count, distinct from `organization_usage.seats_used` |
36	| `current_period_start` | TEXT | no | — | |
37	| `current_period_end` | TEXT | no | — | |
38	| `cancel_at` | TEXT | yes | — | scheduled cancellation, null if not canceling |
39	| `created_at` | TEXT | no | now | |
40	| `updated_at` | TEXT | no | now | |
41	
42	**Indexes**
43	
44	| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
45	|---|---|---|---|
46	| `subscriptions_org_idx` | `org_id` | no | the per-org lookup — not declared unique here even though REQ-130 states "exactly one subscription per organization" |
47	
48	**Invariants**
49	
50	- **Every organization has exactly one subscription (REQ-130)**, but `subscriptions_org_idx`
51	  is a plain `index`, not a `uniqueIndex` — unlike `organization_usage`, which enforces its 1:1
52	  relationship structurally by making `org_id` the primary key itself. This is worth flagging
53	  precisely: the "exactly one" guarantee for `subscriptions` is a requirement and presumably a
54	  service-level discipline (`BillingService` never calling `insertSubscription` for an org that
55	  already has one), not a database-level constraint the way `organization_usage`'s shape makes
56	  it. A row's absence for a given `org_id`, or more than one, would not be caught by this
57	  table's schema alone.
58	- **`seats` (contracted) is distinct from `organization_usage.seats_used` (actual active
59	  members, REQ-133).** The former is what the org is billed for; the latter is what it is
60	  actually consuming. `updateSeatCount` changes the contracted number; it does not touch
61	  `organization_usage`.
62	- **Downgrades are refused while usage exceeds the target plan (REQ-141).** `BillingService`
63	  checks `organization_usage` against the target plan's `PLAN_LIMITS` entry before allowing
64	  `updateSubscriptionPlan` to move `plan` downward — this table's own columns carry no
65	  constraint preventing an inconsistent downgrade; the check happens entirely in the service
66	  layer, reading two tables (`subscriptions` and `organization_usage`) together.
67	- **Trials expire on a schedule (REQ-142).** `listTrialsEndingBefore` supports a scheduled job
68	  that finds subscriptions whose trial period is ending and falls them back to `free` — the
69	  actual trial end marker lives on `organizations.trial_ends_at`, not on this table, which is
70	  worth noting as a small cross-table split: `subscriptions.status` reflects billing state
71	  broadly, while the specific trial countdown timestamp is denormalized onto `organizations`.
72	
73	**Read and write paths**
74	
75	`src/server/repositories/subscription-repository.ts`: `findSubscription`, `insertSubscription`,
76	`updateSubscriptionPlan` (REQ-140's `billing.plan_changed` event source), `updateSeatCount`,
77	`cancelSubscription`, `listTrialsEndingBefore` (REQ-142). `BillingService` is the sole caller.
78	
79	## `invoices`
80	
81	**Drizzle export:** `invoices` in `src/server/db/schema/billing.ts`
82	**Soft delete:** no — append-only billing record
83	**Tenant column:** `org_id`
84	
85	| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
86	|---|---|---|---|---|
87	| `id` | TEXT | no (PK) | — | ULID, typed a plain string (no dedicated `InvoiceId` appears in `AnyId`'s fourteen branded types) |
88	| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | |
89	| `number` | TEXT | no | — | human-facing invoice number |
90	| `amount_cents` | INTEGER | no | — | monetary amounts stored as integer cents, never floating point |
91	| `currency` | TEXT | no | `'usd'` | |
92	| `period_start` | TEXT | no | — | |
93	| `period_end` | TEXT | no | — | REQ-143, one invoice per billing period |
94	| `paid_at` | TEXT | yes | — | null until paid |
95	| `created_at` | TEXT | no | now | |
96	| `updated_at` | TEXT | no | now | |
97	
98	**Indexes**
99	
100	| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
101	|---|---|---|---|
102	| `invoices_org_period_idx` | `org_id, period_start` | no | listing an org's invoice history in period order |
103	
104	**Invariants**
105	
106	- **One invoice per billing period per organization (REQ-143)**, though — the same pattern as
107	  `subscriptions` — there is no unique index enforcing `(org_id, period_start)` uniqueness at
108	  the database level; `invoices_org_period_idx` is a plain index, and the "one per period"
109	  guarantee is a generation-job discipline, not a schema constraint.
110	- **`amount_cents` is an integer, never a floating-point or decimal type** — SQLite has no
111	  fixed-point decimal type, and storing cents as an integer avoids floating-point rounding
112	  error in monetary arithmetic entirely, a common and deliberate pattern this schema follows
113	  consistently (there is no other monetary column anywhere in the schema, so this is the one
114	  place the convention is exercised).
115	- `InvoiceRow`'s `id` field is typed as a plain string in `NewInvoiceRow`/`InvoiceRow`'s
116	  inferred types — worth noting as a small gap relative to **ADR-015**'s branded-id discipline,
117	  since `AnyId`'s explicit fourteen-member union in `src/types/common.ts` does not include an
118	  `InvoiceId`, unlike every other entity table's primary key documented across this dictionary.
119	
120	**Read and write paths**
121	
122	`src/server/repositories/invoice-repository.ts`: `listInvoices`, `insertInvoice`,
123	`findInvoice`. `BillingService` generates invoices on a schedule tied to each subscription's
124	billing period; there is no `updateInvoice`-shaped function beyond `insertInvoice` — an
125	invoice, once generated, is presumably marked paid through a narrower mechanism not exposed as
126	a separate repository function in this file's listed surface, or `paid_at` is set as part of a
127	payment-webhook-driven flow this schema's repository layer does not itself model in detail.
128	
129	## Plan limits are not a database table
130	
131	**ADR-010**'s title, "declare every plan quota in one table," could be misread as describing a
132	database table this schema should contain, and it is worth being explicit that no such table
133	exists —
134	there is no `plan_limits` table in any of the eleven schema files, and REQ-132's "plan quotas
135	are declared in one place" is satisfied by `PLAN_LIMITS`, a `Readonly<Record<PlanId,
136	PlanLimits>>` constant object in `src/config/plan-limits.ts`, not by a queryable database
137	table. Reading `PLAN_LIMITS[org.plan]` is how every quota check in the codebase — seat count
138	against `organization_usage.seatsUsed`, project count against `projects` rows, issue count
139	against `issues` rows, webhook count against `webhook_endpoints` rows — gets its ceiling.
140	`UNLIMITED` is `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` (REQ-137), used for the enterprise plan's `seats`,
141	`projects`, `issuesPerProject`, and `webhooks` fields, which is why comparisons against these
142	limits use ordinary numeric `>=`/`<` rather than a sentinel value requiring special-case
143	handling — `Infinity` composes correctly with normal arithmetic and comparison, which is
144	exactly why REQ-137 specifies it rather than, say, `-1` or `null` as the unlimited marker.
145	`REQ-138`'s "exceeding a quota produces `plan_limit_exceeded`, not a crash" and `REQ-139`'s
146	`billing.limit_exceeded` event are both consequences of quota checks reading `PLAN_LIMITS`
147	against the live counted or cached (`organization_usage`) numbers documented in this dictionary
148	— but the limits themselves are code, not data, and this dictionary's "define no ids" scope
149	means `PLAN_LIMITS`'s exact values are summarized here (see `docs/db/index.md`'s row-count
150	expectations table) rather than fully reproduced, since it is config, not schema.

org is on, what it is billed) rather than the *consumption* side.

## `subscriptions`

**Drizzle export:** `subscriptions` in `src/server/db/schema/billing.ts`
**Soft delete:** no — a subscription's lifecycle is its own `status` enum, not archiving
**Tenant column:** `org_id`

| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | TEXT | no (PK) | — | ULID, typed `SubscriptionId` |
| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | REQ-130, exactly one subscription per organization |
| `plan` | TEXT | no | `'free'` | enum: `free`, `starter`, `growth`, `enterprise` — the same four-value ladder as `organizations.plan` (REQ-131) |
| `interval` | TEXT | no | `'monthly'` | enum: `monthly`, `annual` |
| `status` | TEXT | no | `'trialing'` | enum: `trialing`, `active`, `past_due`, `canceled` |
| `seats` | INTEGER | no | `1` | contracted seat count, distinct from `organization_usage.seats_used` |
| `current_period_start` | TEXT | no | — | |
| `current_period_end` | TEXT | no | — | |
| `cancel_at` | TEXT | yes | — | scheduled cancellation, null if not canceling |
| `created_at` | TEXT | no | now | |
| `updated_at` | TEXT | no | now | |

**Indexes**

| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
|---|---|---|---|
| `subscriptions_org_idx` | `org_id` | no | the per-org lookup — not declared unique here even though REQ-130 states "exactly one subscription per organization" |

**Invariants**

- **Every organization has exactly one subscription (REQ-130)**, but `subscriptions_org_idx`
  is a plain `index`, not a `uniqueIndex` — unlike `organization_usage`, which enforces its 1:1
  relationship structurally by making `org_id` the primary key itself. This is worth flagging
  precisely: the "exactly one" guarantee for `subscriptions` is a requirement and presumably a
  service-level discipline (`BillingService` never calling `insertSubscription` for an org that
  already has one), not a database-level constraint the way `organization_usage`'s shape makes
  it. A row's absence for a given `org_id`, or more than one, would not be caught by this
  table's schema alone.
- **`seats` (contracted) is distinct from `organization_usage.seats_used` (actual active
  members, REQ-133).** The former is what the org is billed for; the latter is what it is
  actually consuming. `updateSeatCount` changes the contracted number; it does not touch
  `organization_usage`.
- **Downgrades are refused while usage exceeds the target plan (REQ-141).** `BillingService`
  checks `organization_usage` against the target plan's `PLAN_LIMITS` entry before allowing
  `updateSubscriptionPlan` to move `plan` downward — this table's own columns carry no
  constraint preventing an inconsistent downgrade; the check happens entirely in the service
  layer, reading two tables (`subscriptions` and `organization_usage`) together.
- **Trials expire on a schedule (REQ-142).** `listTrialsEndingBefore` supports a scheduled job
  that finds subscriptions whose trial period is ending and falls them back to `free` — the
  actual trial end marker lives on `organizations.trial_ends_at`, not on this table, which is
  worth noting as a small cross-table split: `subscriptions.status` reflects billing state
  broadly, while the specific trial countdown timestamp is denormalized onto `organizations`.

**Read and write paths**

`src/server/repositories/subscription-repository.ts`: `findSubscription`, `insertSubscription`,
`updateSubscriptionPlan` (REQ-140's `billing.plan_changed` event source), `updateSeatCount`,
`cancelSubscription`, `listTrialsEndingBefore` (REQ-142). `BillingService` is the sole caller.

## `invoices`

**Drizzle export:** `invoices` in `src/server/db/schema/billing.ts`
**Soft delete:** no — append-only billing record
**Tenant column:** `org_id`

| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | TEXT | no (PK) | — | ULID, typed a plain string (no dedicated `InvoiceId` appears in `AnyId`'s fourteen branded types) |
| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | |
| `number` | TEXT | no | — | human-facing invoice number |
| `amount_cents` | INTEGER | no | — | monetary amounts stored as integer cents, never floating point |
| `currency` | TEXT | no | `'usd'` | |
| `period_start` | TEXT | no | — | |
| `period_end` | TEXT | no | — | REQ-143, one invoice per billing period |
| `paid_at` | TEXT | yes | — | null until paid |
| `created_at` | TEXT | no | now | |
| `updated_at` | TEXT | no | now | |

**Indexes**

| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
|---|---|---|---|
| `invoices_org_period_idx` | `org_id, period_start` | no | listing an org's invoice history in period order |

**Invariants**

- **One invoice per billing period per organization (REQ-143)**, though — the same pattern as
  `subscriptions` — there is no unique index enforcing `(org_id, period_start)` uniqueness at
  the database level; `invoices_org_period_idx` is a plain index, and the "one per period"
  guarantee is a generation-job discipline, not a schema constraint.
- **`amount_cents` is an integer, never a floating-point or decimal type** — SQLite has no
  fixed-point decimal type, and storing cents as an integer avoids floating-point rounding
  error in monetary arithmetic entirely, a common and deliberate pattern this schema follows
  consistently (there is no other monetary column anywhere in the schema, so this is the one
  place the convention is exercised).
- `InvoiceRow`'s `id` field is typed as a plain string in `NewInvoiceRow`/`InvoiceRow`'s
  inferred types — worth noting as a small gap relative to **ADR-015**'s branded-id discipline,
  since `AnyId`'s explicit fourteen-member union in `src/types/common.ts` does not include an
  `InvoiceId`, unlike every other entity table's primary key documented across this dictionary.

**Read and write paths**

`src/server/repositories/invoice-repository.ts`: `listInvoices`, `insertInvoice`,
`findInvoice`. `BillingService` generates invoices on a schedule tied to each subscription's
billing period; there is no `updateInvoice`-shaped function beyond `insertInvoice` — an
invoice, once generated, is presumably marked paid through a narrower mechanism not exposed as
a separate repository function in this file's listed surface, or `paid_at` is set as part of a
payment-webhook-driven flow this schema's repository layer does not itself model in detail.

## Plan limits are not a database table

**ADR-010**'s title, "declare every plan quota in one table," could be misread as describing a
database table this schema should contain, and it is worth being explicit that no such table
exists —
there is no `plan_limits` table in any of the eleven schema files, and REQ-132's "plan quotas
are declared in one place" is satisfied by `PLAN_LIMITS`, a `Readonly<Record<PlanId,
PlanLimits>>` constant object in `src/config/plan-limits.ts`, not by a queryable database
table. Reading `PLAN_LIMITS[org.plan]` is how every quota check in the codebase — seat count
against `organization_usage.seatsUsed`, project count against `projects` rows, issue count
against `issues` rows, webhook count against `webhook_endpoints` rows — gets its ceiling.
`UNLIMITED` is `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` (REQ-137), used for the enterprise plan's `seats`,
`projects`, `issuesPerProject`, and `webhooks` fields, which is why comparisons against these
limits use ordinary numeric `>=`/`<` rather than a sentinel value requiring special-case
handling — `Infinity` composes correctly with normal arithmetic and comparison, which is
exactly why REQ-137 specifies it rather than, say, `-1` or `null` as the unlimited marker.
`REQ-138`'s "exceeding a quota produces `plan_limit_exceeded`, not a crash" and `REQ-139`'s
`billing.limit_exceeded` event are both consequences of quota checks reading `PLAN_LIMITS`
against the live counted or cached (`organization_usage`) numbers documented in this dictionary
— but the limits themselves are code, not data, and this dictionary's "define no ids" scope
means `PLAN_LIMITS`'s exact values are summarized here (see `docs/db/index.md`'s row-count
expectations table) rather than fully reproduced, since it is config, not schema.

1	---
2	title: Notifications and activity
3	status: approved
4	owners: [platform-team]
5	last_updated: 2026-06-20
6	related: [REQ-110, REQ-111, REQ-114, REQ-115, REQ-116, REQ-117, REQ-119, REQ-220, REQ-221, REQ-222, REQ-223, REQ-227, REQ-228, REQ-229, REQ-231, ADR-005, ADR-006, ADR-008, ADR-022, DES-204, DES-050]
7	---
8	
9	## Purpose
10	
11	This file documents `notifications`, `notification_preferences`, and `activity_events` —
12	three tables that together are the schema's expression of Taskflow's in-process event bus
13	(ADR-005). Every domain mutation elsewhere in the schema (an issue created, a comment posted,
14	a member invited) is expected to emit an event, and these three tables are where two
15	different consumers of that same event stream land: `notifications`/`notification_preferences`
16	turn events into per-recipient, per-channel messages (`notifications.ts`), while
17	`activity_events` (`activity.ts`) turns the same events into an immutable audit log
18	(REQ-221, ADR-022). Reading them together is the fastest way to see the one-event,
19	two-consumers shape of the event bus at the schema level.
20	
21	## `notifications`
22	
23	**Drizzle export:** `notifications` in `src/server/db/schema/notifications.ts`
24	**Soft delete:** no — a notification is read or unread, never archived
25	**Tenant column:** `org_id`
26	
27	| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
28	|---|---|---|---|---|
29	| `id` | TEXT | no (PK) | — | ULID, typed `NotificationId` |
30	| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | REQ-110, per organization |
31	| `recipient_id` | TEXT | no | — | typed `UserId`; REQ-110, per recipient |
32	| `kind` | TEXT | no | — | one of eleven literal enum values (see below) |
33	| `title` | TEXT | no | — | |
34	| `body` | TEXT | no | — | |
35	| `href` | TEXT | no | — | deep link the notification resolves to |
36	| `actor_id` | TEXT | yes | — | typed `UserId`; the user whose action triggered it, null for system-generated notifications |
37	| `read_at` | TEXT | yes | — | null means unread |
38	| `channels` | TEXT | no | `'["in_app"]'` | JSON array of `NotificationChannel` values |
39	| `created_at` | TEXT | no | now | |
40	| `updated_at` | TEXT | no | now | bumped on `markRead`/`markAllRead` |
41	
42	**Indexes**
43	
44	| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
45	|---|---|---|---|
46	| `notifications_org_recipient_idx` | `org_id, recipient_id` | no | the per-recipient inbox query, REQ-118 |
47	| `notifications_org_read_idx` | `org_id, read_at` | no | REQ-117's per-org unread-count computation |
48	
49	**Invariants**
50	
51	- **`kind` is a closed vocabulary** declared as a module-level `NOTIFICATION_KINDS` constant
52	  (`issue_assigned`, `issue_status_changed`, `issue_due_soon`, `issue_overdue`,
53	  `comment_created`, `comment_mention`, `member_invited`, `member_joined`,
54	  `project_archived`, `plan_limit_reached`, `digest_ready`) and reused, verbatim, as the enum
55	  for `notification_preferences.kind` below — this is the one place in the schema where two
56	  different tables' `enum` constraints are generated from the same shared constant rather than
57	  independently declared, which keeps the notification-kind vocabulary and the preference-kind
58	  vocabulary from drifting apart.
59	- **Actors are never notified about their own actions (REQ-114).** This is a filter applied
60	  before `insertNotification`/`insertNotifications` runs, not something the schema itself can
61	  express — a `notifications` row with `recipient_id = actor_id` is not structurally forbidden,
62	  only avoided by `NotificationService`'s fan-out logic.
63	- **Recipients may only manage their own notifications (REQ-118).** `markRead`/`markAllRead`
64	  are expected to be called with the acting user's own id as `recipient_id`, checked by
65	  `NotificationService`, not by a row-level constraint.
66	- **This table is never archived and never pruned by `archived_at`-style logic** — its
67	  lifecycle is entirely the `read_at` state machine (unread → read), and cleanup, where it
68	  exists, would follow the same retention-window pattern activity events use, though no
69	  `purgeNotifications`-equivalent function appears in `notification-repository.ts`'s exported
70	  surface — notifications appear to accumulate without a documented pruning path in this
71	  schema's current repository functions.
72	
73	**Read and write paths**
74	
75	`src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts`: `listNotifications`, `countUnread`
76	(REQ-117), `insertNotification` / `insertNotifications` (singular and batch — the batch form
77	supports fanning one event out to many recipients in one write), `markRead`, `markAllRead`,
78	`listUnreadSince` (feeds the digest window, REQ-121). `NotificationService` is the sole caller,
79	and it is the event-bus subscriber that turns domain events into rows here.
80	
81	## `notification_preferences`
82	
83	**Drizzle export:** `notificationPreferences` in `src/server/db/schema/notifications.ts`
84	**Soft delete:** no
85	**Tenant column:** `org_id`
86	
87	| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
88	|---|---|---|---|---|
89	| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | |
90	| `user_id` | TEXT | no | — | typed `UserId` |
91	| `kind` | TEXT | no | — | same `NOTIFICATION_KINDS` enum as `notifications.kind` |
92	| `in_app` | INTEGER (boolean) | no | `true` | |
93	| `email` | INTEGER (boolean) | no | `true` | |
94	| `digest_only` | INTEGER (boolean) | no | `false` | routes this kind to the digest rather than immediate email |
95	
96	**Indexes**
97	
98	| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
99	|---|---|---|---|
100	| `notification_preferences_pk` | `org_id, user_id, kind` | yes | one preference row per user, per org, per notification kind — REQ-115's "per channel and per event class" |
101	
102	**Invariants**
103	
104	- **Preferences are per (org, user, kind) triple, not global to the user.** A user's email
105	  preference for `comment_mention` in one organization is independent of their preference for
106	  the same kind in a different organization — consistent with `members` being per-org and
107	  notification fan-out being org-scoped.
108	- **No row means the default preference applies** — `getPreference` presumably falls back to
109	  the column defaults (`in_app: true, email: true, digest_only: false`) when no explicit row
110	  exists for a given `(org, user, kind)`, since there is no `insertMember`-triggered row
111	  creation implied anywhere in this schema for every possible kind × member combination; that
112	  would be an eleven-times multiplier on `members` row count for no benefit when defaults
113	  suffice.
114	
115	**Read and write paths**
116	
117	`src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts`: `listPreferences`,
118	`getPreference`, `upsertPreference`, `listDigestSubscribers` (feeds REQ-119's digest batching
119	by finding who has `digest_only` set, or who simply has email enabled and a digest is due).
120	`NotificationService` reads preferences before fan-out to decide which channels a given kind
121	should actually notify through for a given recipient.
122	
123	## `activity_events`
124	
125	**Drizzle export:** `activityEvents` in `src/server/db/schema/activity.ts`
126	**Soft delete:** no — this table is append-only and immutable by design (REQ-221)
127	**Tenant column:** `org_id`
128	
129	| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
130	|---|---|---|---|---|
131	| `id` | TEXT | no (PK) | — | ULID, typed `ActivityId` |
132	| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | REQ-220 |
133	| `action` | TEXT | no | — | free-text action identifier (not a closed schema enum, unlike `notifications.kind`) |
134	| `actor_id` | TEXT | yes | — | typed `UserId`; null for system-triggered activity |
135	| `subject_kind` | TEXT | no | — | enum: `organization`, `project`, `issue`, `comment`, `member`, `subscription`, `feature_flag` |
136	| `subject_id` | TEXT | no | — | the id of the row the event concerns, typed generically as a plain string since it can be any of the seven subject kinds |
137	| `project_id` | TEXT | yes | — | denormalized, present when the subject has a natural project association, for project-scoped activity views |
138	| `summary` | TEXT | no | — | human-readable one-line description |
139	| `metadata` | TEXT | no | `'{}'` | JSON object of scalar metadata, e.g. before/after values for REQ-034's role-change audit |
140	| `occurred_at` | TEXT | no | — | REQ-229's pagination sort key; distinct from `created_at`, since this table has no `created_at`/`updated_at` pair at all |
141	
142	**Indexes**
143	
144	| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
145	|---|---|---|---|
146	| `activity_org_occurred_idx` | `org_id, occurred_at` | no | REQ-229's time-ordered pagination |
147	| `activity_org_action_idx` | `org_id, action` | no | filtering the feed by action type |
148	| `activity_org_subject_idx` | `org_id, subject_kind, subject_id` | no | REQ-223's "queryable by subject" — jumping to an issue's or project's own activity history |
149	
150	**Invariants**
151	
152	- **Rows are immutable once written (REQ-221)** — there is no `updateActivity`-shaped
153	  function in `activity-repository.ts`'s exported surface; the only writes are `insertActivity`
154	  and the retention-driven `purgeActivityBefore`. No `updated_at` column exists on this table
155	  at all, which is itself evidence of the immutability invariant at the schema level, not just
156	  a convention: there is nothing to bump.
157	- **Activity capture must not fail the originating write (REQ-228).** This is a
158	  reliability/ordering property of how `ActivityService` is invoked relative to the mutation it
159	  records, not something the `activity_events` schema itself enforces — worth noting here
160	  because it explains why activity insertion is typically a best-effort side effect fired from
161	  the event bus (ADR-022) rather than wrapped in the same transaction as the primary mutation;
162	  `better-sqlite3`'s single-writer, synchronous model (ADR-002) makes a failed activity insert
163	  after a successful primary write a real possibility this requirement is guarding against.
164	- **`occurred_at`, not `created_at`, is the canonical timestamp.** This is a deliberate
165	  divergence from every other table's `timestampColumns` pattern — `activity_events` spreads
166	  only `tenantColumns` from `_shared.ts`, not `timestampColumns`, and declares `occurred_at`
167	  itself instead, because the moment an event *occurred* (which could, in principle, differ
168	  from the moment the row was inserted, though in practice they are the same instant for this
169	  synchronous event bus) is the semantically meaningful timestamp for an audit log.
170	- **Retention follows the plan's window (REQ-227), enforced by `purgeActivityBefore` (REQ-231),
171	  a scheduled cleanup job — not automatic expiry.** Rows older than
172	  `PLAN_LIMITS[org.plan].retentionDays` are deleted, but only when the cleanup job runs; between
173	  runs, activity older than the nominal retention window can still be present.
174	- **Reading the feed requires member access (REQ-224); exporting it requires admin (REQ-225);
175	  the whole feature is gated by a feature flag (REQ-226).** All three are authorization/rollout
176	  concerns enforced by `ActivityService` via `can()`/feature-flag checks, not by this table's
177	  own columns.
178	
179	**Read and write paths**
180	
181	`src/server/repositories/activity-repository.ts`: `insertActivity`, `listActivity` (keyset-
182	paginated by `occurred_at`, REQ-229), `listActivityForSubject` (REQ-223), `purgeActivityBefore`
183	(REQ-231's scheduled retention cleanup). `ActivityService` is the sole caller, subscribing to
184	the event bus (ADR-005) the same way `NotificationService` does — the two services are
185	independent consumers of the same underlying domain events, which is why `notifications` and
186	`activity_events` end up looking structurally similar (both carry `actor_id`, both reference a
187	subject) while serving different purposes: one is a per-recipient inbox, the other is a
188	tenant-wide, immutable log.
189	
190	**Notes**
191	
192	The absence of a shared "events" table that both `notifications` and `activity_events` read
193	from is worth being explicit about: there is no `domain_events` table in this schema at all.
194	The event bus (ADR-005) is in-process and in-memory — events are dispatched to subscribers
195	directly as they happen, and `notifications`/`activity_events` are each subscriber's own
196	durable record of what it did in response, not two views over one persisted event log. This
197	means an event that fails to reach one subscriber (say, activity capture failing per REQ-228's
198	own framing) would not corrupt or block the other subscriber's record, since there is no shared
199	row either of them depends on. It also means the two tables can, and do, evolve independently:
200	`notifications` gained the `channels` JSON column without any equivalent change to

| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | REQ-110, per organization |
| `recipient_id` | TEXT | no | — | typed `UserId`; REQ-110, per recipient |
| `kind` | TEXT | no | — | one of eleven literal enum values (see below) |
| `title` | TEXT | no | — | |
| `body` | TEXT | no | — | |
| `href` | TEXT | no | — | deep link the notification resolves to |
| `actor_id` | TEXT | yes | — | typed `UserId`; the user whose action triggered it, null for system-generated notifications |
| `read_at` | TEXT | yes | — | null means unread |
| `channels` | TEXT | no | `'["in_app"]'` | JSON array of `NotificationChannel` values |
| `created_at` | TEXT | no | now | |
| `updated_at` | TEXT | no | now | bumped on `markRead`/`markAllRead` |

**Indexes**

| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
|---|---|---|---|
| `notifications_org_recipient_idx` | `org_id, recipient_id` | no | the per-recipient inbox query, REQ-118 |
| `notifications_org_read_idx` | `org_id, read_at` | no | REQ-117's per-org unread-count computation |

**Invariants**

- **`kind` is a closed vocabulary** declared as a module-level `NOTIFICATION_KINDS` constant
  (`issue_assigned`, `issue_status_changed`, `issue_due_soon`, `issue_overdue`,
  `comment_created`, `comment_mention`, `member_invited`, `member_joined`,
  `project_archived`, `plan_limit_reached`, `digest_ready`) and reused, verbatim, as the enum
  for `notification_preferences.kind` below — this is the one place in the schema where two
  different tables' `enum` constraints are generated from the same shared constant rather than
  independently declared, which keeps the notification-kind vocabulary and the preference-kind
  vocabulary from drifting apart.
- **Actors are never notified about their own actions (REQ-114).** This is a filter applied
  before `insertNotification`/`insertNotifications` runs, not something the schema itself can
  express — a `notifications` row with `recipient_id = actor_id` is not structurally forbidden,
  only avoided by `NotificationService`'s fan-out logic.
- **Recipients may only manage their own notifications (REQ-118).** `markRead`/`markAllRead`
  are expected to be called with the acting user's own id as `recipient_id`, checked by
  `NotificationService`, not by a row-level constraint.
- **This table is never archived and never pruned by `archived_at`-style logic** — its
  lifecycle is entirely the `read_at` state machine (unread → read), and cleanup, where it
  exists, would follow the same retention-window pattern activity events use, though no
  `purgeNotifications`-equivalent function appears in `notification-repository.ts`'s exported
  surface — notifications appear to accumulate without a documented pruning path in this
  schema's current repository functions.

**Read and write paths**

`src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts`: `listNotifications`, `countUnread`
(REQ-117), `insertNotification` / `insertNotifications` (singular and batch — the batch form
supports fanning one event out to many recipients in one write), `markRead`, `markAllRead`,
`listUnreadSince` (feeds the digest window, REQ-121). `NotificationService` is the sole caller,
and it is the event-bus subscriber that turns domain events into rows here.

## `notification_preferences`

**Drizzle export:** `notificationPreferences` in `src/server/db/schema/notifications.ts`
**Soft delete:** no
**Tenant column:** `org_id`

| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | |
| `user_id` | TEXT | no | — | typed `UserId` |
| `kind` | TEXT | no | — | same `NOTIFICATION_KINDS` enum as `notifications.kind` |
| `in_app` | INTEGER (boolean) | no | `true` | |
| `email` | INTEGER (boolean) | no | `true` | |
| `digest_only` | INTEGER (boolean) | no | `false` | routes this kind to the digest rather than immediate email |

**Indexes**

| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
|---|---|---|---|
| `notification_preferences_pk` | `org_id, user_id, kind` | yes | one preference row per user, per org, per notification kind — REQ-115's "per channel and per event class" |

**Invariants**

- **Preferences are per (org, user, kind) triple, not global to the user.** A user's email
  preference for `comment_mention` in one organization is independent of their preference for
  the same kind in a different organization — consistent with `members` being per-org and
  notification fan-out being org-scoped.
- **No row means the default preference applies** — `getPreference` presumably falls back to
  the column defaults (`in_app: true, email: true, digest_only: false`) when no explicit row
  exists for a given `(org, user, kind)`, since there is no `insertMember`-triggered row
  creation implied anywhere in this schema for every possible kind × member combination; that
  would be an eleven-times multiplier on `members` row count for no benefit when defaults
  suffice.

**Read and write paths**

`src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts`: `listPreferences`,
`getPreference`, `upsertPreference`, `listDigestSubscribers` (feeds REQ-119's digest batching
by finding who has `digest_only` set, or who simply has email enabled and a digest is due).
`NotificationService` reads preferences before fan-out to decide which channels a given kind
should actually notify through for a given recipient.

## `activity_events`

**Drizzle export:** `activityEvents` in `src/server/db/schema/activity.ts`
**Soft delete:** no — this table is append-only and immutable by design (REQ-221)
**Tenant column:** `org_id`

| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | TEXT | no (PK) | — | ULID, typed `ActivityId` |
| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | REQ-220 |
| `action` | TEXT | no | — | free-text action identifier (not a closed schema enum, unlike `notifications.kind`) |
| `actor_id` | TEXT | yes | — | typed `UserId`; null for system-triggered activity |
| `subject_kind` | TEXT | no | — | enum: `organization`, `project`, `issue`, `comment`, `member`, `subscription`, `feature_flag` |
| `subject_id` | TEXT | no | — | the id of the row the event concerns, typed generically as a plain string since it can be any of the seven subject kinds |
| `project_id` | TEXT | yes | — | denormalized, present when the subject has a natural project association, for project-scoped activity views |
| `summary` | TEXT | no | — | human-readable one-line description |
| `metadata` | TEXT | no | `'{}'` | JSON object of scalar metadata, e.g. before/after values for REQ-034's role-change audit |
| `occurred_at` | TEXT | no | — | REQ-229's pagination sort key; distinct from `created_at`, since this table has no `created_at`/`updated_at` pair at all |

**Indexes**

| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
|---|---|---|---|
| `activity_org_occurred_idx` | `org_id, occurred_at` | no | REQ-229's time-ordered pagination |
| `activity_org_action_idx` | `org_id, action` | no | filtering the feed by action type |
| `activity_org_subject_idx` | `org_id, subject_kind, subject_id` | no | REQ-223's "queryable by subject" — jumping to an issue's or project's own activity history |

**Invariants**

- **Rows are immutable once written (REQ-221)** — there is no `updateActivity`-shaped
  function in `activity-repository.ts`'s exported surface; the only writes are `insertActivity`
  and the retention-driven `purgeActivityBefore`. No `updated_at` column exists on this table
  at all, which is itself evidence of the immutability invariant at the schema level, not just
  a convention: there is nothing to bump.
- **Activity capture must not fail the originating write (REQ-228).** This is a
  reliability/ordering property of how `ActivityService` is invoked relative to the mutation it
  records, not something the `activity_events` schema itself enforces — worth noting here
  because it explains why activity insertion is typically a best-effort side effect fired from
  the event bus (ADR-022) rather than wrapped in the same transaction as the primary mutation;
  `better-sqlite3`'s single-writer, synchronous model (ADR-002) makes a failed activity insert
  after a successful primary write a real possibility this requirement is guarding against.
- **`occurred_at`, not `created_at`, is the canonical timestamp.** This is a deliberate
  divergence from every other table's `timestampColumns` pattern — `activity_events` spreads
  only `tenantColumns` from `_shared.ts`, not `timestampColumns`, and declares `occurred_at`
  itself instead, because the moment an event *occurred* (which could, in principle, differ
  from the moment the row was inserted, though in practice they are the same instant for this
  synchronous event bus) is the semantically meaningful timestamp for an audit log.
- **Retention follows the plan's window (REQ-227), enforced by `purgeActivityBefore` (REQ-231),
  a scheduled cleanup job — not automatic expiry.** Rows older than
  `PLAN_LIMITS[org.plan].retentionDays` are deleted, but only when the cleanup job runs; between
  runs, activity older than the nominal retention window can still be present.
- **Reading the feed requires member access (REQ-224); exporting it requires admin (REQ-225);
  the whole feature is gated by a feature flag (REQ-226).** All three are authorization/rollout
  concerns enforced by `ActivityService` via `can()`/feature-flag checks, not by this table's
  own columns.

**Read and write paths**

`src/server/repositories/activity-repository.ts`: `insertActivity`, `listActivity` (keyset-
paginated by `occurred_at`, REQ-229), `listActivityForSubject` (REQ-223), `purgeActivityBefore`
(REQ-231's scheduled retention cleanup). `ActivityService` is the sole caller, subscribing to
the event bus (ADR-005) the same way `NotificationService` does — the two services are
independent consumers of the same underlying domain events, which is why `notifications` and
`activity_events` end up looking structurally similar (both carry `actor_id`, both reference a
subject) while serving different purposes: one is a per-recipient inbox, the other is a
tenant-wide, immutable log.

**Notes**

The absence of a shared "events" table that both `notifications` and `activity_events` read
from is worth being explicit about: there is no `domain_events` table in this schema at all.
The event bus (ADR-005) is in-process and in-memory — events are dispatched to subscribers
directly as they happen, and `notifications`/`activity_events` are each subscriber's own
durable record of what it did in response, not two views over one persisted event log. This
means an event that fails to reach one subscriber (say, activity capture failing per REQ-228's
own framing) would not corrupt or block the other subscriber's record, since there is no shared
row either of them depends on. It also means the two tables can, and do, evolve independently:
`notifications` gained the `channels` JSON column without any equivalent change to

1	import { index, integer, sqliteTable, text, uniqueIndex } from "drizzle-orm/sqlite-core";
2	import { idColumn, tenantColumns, timestampColumns } from "./_shared";
3	
4	const NOTIFICATION_KINDS = [
5	  "issue_assigned",
6	  "issue_status_changed",
7	  "issue_due_soon",
8	  "issue_overdue",
9	  "comment_created",
10	  "comment_mention",
11	  "member_invited",
12	  "member_joined",
13	  "project_archived",
14	  "plan_limit_reached",
15	  "digest_ready",
16	] as const;
17	
18	export const notifications = sqliteTable(
19	  "notifications",
20	  {
21	    id: idColumn(),
22	    ...tenantColumns,
23	    recipientId: text("recipient_id").notNull(),
24	    kind: text("kind", { enum: NOTIFICATION_KINDS }).notNull(),
25	    title: text("title").notNull(),
26	    body: text("body").notNull(),
27	    href: text("href").notNull(),
28	    actorId: text("actor_id"),
29	    readAt: text("read_at"),
30	    /** JSON array of `NotificationChannel`. */
31	    channels: text("channels").notNull().default('["in_app"]'),
32	    ...timestampColumns,
33	  },
34	  (table) => [
35	    index("notifications_org_recipient_idx").on(table.orgId, table.recipientId),
36	    index("notifications_org_read_idx").on(table.orgId, table.readAt),
37	  ],
38	);
39	
40	export const notificationPreferences = sqliteTable(
41	  "notification_preferences",
42	  {
43	    ...tenantColumns,
44	    userId: text("user_id").notNull(),
45	    kind: text("kind", { enum: NOTIFICATION_KINDS }).notNull(),
46	    inApp: integer("in_app", { mode: "boolean" }).notNull().default(true),
47	    email: integer("email", { mode: "boolean" }).notNull().default(true),
48	    digestOnly: integer("digest_only", { mode: "boolean" })
49	      .notNull()
50	      .default(false),
51	  },
52	  (table) => [
53	    uniqueIndex("notification_preferences_pk").on(
54	      table.orgId,
55	      table.userId,
56	      table.kind,
57	    ),
58	  ],
59	);
60	
61	export type NotificationRow = typeof notifications.$inferSelect;
62	export type NewNotificationRow = typeof notifications.$inferInsert;
63	export type NotificationPreferenceRow =
64	  typeof notificationPreferences.$inferSelect;
65

1	---
2	title: Webhooks, search and infrastructure
3	status: approved
4	owners: [platform-team]
5	last_updated: 2026-06-20
6	related: [REQ-150, REQ-153, REQ-154, REQ-155, REQ-156, REQ-157, REQ-158, REQ-161, REQ-170, REQ-171, REQ-172, REQ-174, REQ-176, REQ-179, REQ-180, ADR-006, ADR-008, ADR-011, ADR-017, ADR-018, DES-058]
7	---
8	
9	## Purpose
10	
11	This file documents the four tables declared in `src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts`:
12	`webhook_endpoints`, `webhook_deliveries`, `rate_limit_buckets`, and `search_index`. The
13	grouping in this schema file, and in this dictionary, is functional rather than domain-driven
14	— none of the four tables are part of the issue-tracking or membership domain proper; they are
15	the persisted state behind three pieces of cross-cutting infrastructure: outbound webhook
16	delivery (ADR-018), in-process rate limiting (ADR-011), and a synchronous, denormalized search
17	index (ADR-017).
18	
19	## `webhook_endpoints`
20	
21	**Drizzle export:** `webhookEndpoints` in `src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts`
22	**Soft delete:** no — endpoints are deleted outright, not archived
23	**Tenant column:** `org_id`
24	
25	| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
26	|---|---|---|---|---|
27	| `id` | TEXT | no (PK) | — | ULID, typed `WebhookId` |
28	| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | REQ-150, per organization |
29	| `url` | TEXT | no | — | the receiving endpoint |
30	| `secret` | TEXT | no | — | signs outgoing payloads, REQ-153 |
31	| `event_types` | TEXT | no | `'[]'` | JSON array of `TaskflowEventType`; which events this endpoint subscribes to |
32	| `enabled` | INTEGER (boolean) | no | `true` | REQ-158, disabled endpoints fail fast |
33	| `created_at` | TEXT | no | now | |
34	| `updated_at` | TEXT | no | now | |
35	
36	**Indexes**
37	
38	| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
39	|---|---|---|---|
40	| `webhook_endpoints_org_idx` | `org_id` | no | listing an org's configured endpoints, and the count feeding `PLAN_LIMITS[plan].webhooks` |
41	
42	**Invariants**
43	
44	- **Bounded by the plan's webhook quota (REQ-152)** — `countEndpoints` is checked by
45	  `WebhookService` before `insertEndpoint`, against `PLAN_LIMITS[org.plan].webhooks` (0 for
46	  free, up to unlimited for enterprise).
47	- **`secret` is stored in plaintext in this column** — unlike `sessions.token_hash` or
48	  `invitations.token_hash`, there is no `_hash` suffix on this column and no indication in the
49	  schema file that it is hashed before storage; it needs to be readable in its original form
50	  to sign each outgoing delivery's payload (REQ-153), which is a fundamentally different
51	  requirement from a session or invitation token that only ever needs to be *compared*, never
52	  reproduced.
53	- **`event_types` filters which domain events actually enqueue a delivery for this endpoint** —
54	  an endpoint subscribed to `["issue.created"]` never gets a `webhook_deliveries` row for a
55	  `comment.created` event; that filtering happens in `WebhookService` before
56	  `enqueueDelivery` is called, reading this JSON column.
57	
58	**Read and write paths**
59	
60	`src/server/repositories/webhook-repository.ts`: `listEndpoints`, `insertEndpoint`,
61	`updateEndpoint`, `deleteEndpoint`, `countEndpoints`. `WebhookService` is the sole caller for
62	configuration; endpoint management additionally requires admin (REQ-151), enforced by
63	`can()`, not by this table.
64	
65	## `webhook_deliveries`
66	
67	**Drizzle export:** `webhookDeliveries` in `src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts`
68	**Soft delete:** no — a delivery's outcome is tracked by `status`, not by archiving
69	**Tenant column:** `org_id`
70	
71	| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
72	|---|---|---|---|---|
73	| `id` | TEXT | no (PK) | — | ULID |
74	| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | denormalized alongside `endpoint_id`, per ADR-006 |
75	| `endpoint_id` | TEXT | no | — | typed `WebhookId` |
76	| `event_type` | TEXT | no | — | REQ-160, the event this delivery carries |
77	| `payload` | TEXT | no | — | REQ-160, the full event envelope, serialized |
78	| `status` | TEXT | no | `'pending'` | enum: `pending`, `delivered`, `failed` |
79	| `attempts` | INTEGER | no | `0` | REQ-157's ceiling check, against `WEBHOOK_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5` |
80	| `last_error` | TEXT | yes | — | most recent failure detail, for REQ-159's visibility in settings |
81	| `delivered_at` | TEXT | yes | — | null until a successful delivery |
82	| `created_at` | TEXT | no | now | |
83	| `updated_at` | TEXT | no | now | bumped on every delivery attempt |
84	
85	**Indexes**
86	
87	| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
88	|---|---|---|---|
89	| `webhook_deliveries_org_status_idx` | `org_id, status` | no | the dispatcher's claim query — finding `pending` deliveries to attempt next (REQ-154, REQ-155) |
90	
91	**Invariants**
92	
93	- **Deliveries are queued, never sent inline with the request that triggered them (REQ-154).**
94	  `enqueueDelivery` only ever writes a `pending` row; the actual HTTP call happens in a
95	  separate dispatch pass driven by `claimPendingDeliveries`, which is REQ-155's "claimed in
96	  bounded batches."
97	- **Failed deliveries retry with exponential backoff up to a fixed ceiling (REQ-156,
98	  REQ-157).** `attempts` increments on each try; once it reaches `WEBHOOK_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (5, from
99	  `src/config/constants.ts`), `markDeliveryFailed` presumably sets a terminal `status: 'failed'`
100	  rather than allowing further retries — the backoff *timing* itself is not stored as a column
101	  here (no `next_attempt_at`-style field exists), so the scheduling of *when* the next retry
102	  happens is computed by the dispatcher at claim time from `attempts` and `updated_at`, not
103	  read from a persisted "next attempt due" value.
104	- **Deliveries to a disabled endpoint fail fast (REQ-158)** — `claimPendingDeliveries` or the
105	  dispatch loop is expected to check `webhook_endpoints.enabled` before attempting a delivery,
106	  short-circuiting to a failed status without consuming a retry attempt against a genuinely
107	  unreachable-but-disabled endpoint; this is a cross-table check at dispatch time, not a
108	  constraint expressed within `webhook_deliveries` itself.
109	
110	**Read and write paths**
111	
112	`src/server/repositories/webhook-repository.ts`: `enqueueDelivery`, `claimPendingDeliveries`,
113	`markDelivered`, `markDeliveryFailed`. Same repository file as `webhook_endpoints`, reflecting
114	that the two tables are two halves of one feature (configuration and delivery log) rather than
115	independently owned. `WebhookService` is the sole caller.
116	
117	## `rate_limit_buckets`
118	
119	**Drizzle export:** `rateLimitBuckets` in `src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts`
120	**Soft delete:** no
121	**Tenant column:** `org_id`
122	
123	| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
124	|---|---|---|---|---|
125	| `id` | TEXT | no (PK) | — | ULID |
126	| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | |
127	| `bucket_key` | TEXT | no | — | identifies which rate-limited operation this bucket tracks |
128	| `tokens` | INTEGER | no | — | current token count (token-bucket algorithm) |
129	| `refilled_at` | TEXT | no | — | last refill timestamp |
130	
131	**Indexes**
132	
133	| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
134	|---|---|---|---|
135	| `rate_limit_org_key_idx` | `org_id, bucket_key` | no | the point lookup every rate-limited operation performs before proceeding |
136	
137	**Invariants**
138	
139	- **This table is generic infrastructure, shared across every rate-limited feature in the
140	  product** — the schema file's own comment says it plainly: "Token-bucket state for
141	  `src/lib/rate-limit.ts`, persisted per org+key." Comment creation (REQ-096), password reset
142	  (REQ-208), search queries (REQ-176), and webhook delivery (REQ-161) are four independently
143	  documented requirements that all rate-limit per organization, and this one table backs all
144	  four rather than each feature declaring its own bucket table — `bucket_key` is what
145	  distinguishes one feature's bucket from another's for the same org.
146	- **ADR-011 ("in-process rate limiter") is the design record this table implements.** Being
147	  backed by a SQLite table rather than an in-memory structure is itself notable: it means rate
148	  limit state survives a process restart, at the cost of a database round trip on every
149	  rate-limited operation — a trade-off consistent with this whole application's single-process,
150	  synchronous, in-process-everything architecture (`better-sqlite3` makes that round trip cheap
151	  enough to accept).
152	- No `index` exists on `bucket_key` alone, only the composite `(org_id, bucket_key)` — every
153	  real query needs both, since rate limiting is always scoped to a specific org.
154	
155	**Read and write paths**
156

---
title: Webhooks, search and infrastructure
status: approved
owners: [platform-team]
last_updated: 2026-06-20
related: [REQ-150, REQ-153, REQ-154, REQ-155, REQ-156, REQ-157, REQ-158, REQ-161, REQ-170, REQ-171, REQ-172, REQ-174, REQ-176, REQ-179, REQ-180, ADR-006, ADR-008, ADR-011, ADR-017, ADR-018, DES-058]
---

## Purpose

This file documents the four tables declared in `src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts`:
`webhook_endpoints`, `webhook_deliveries`, `rate_limit_buckets`, and `search_index`. The
grouping in this schema file, and in this dictionary, is functional rather than domain-driven
— none of the four tables are part of the issue-tracking or membership domain proper; they are
the persisted state behind three pieces of cross-cutting infrastructure: outbound webhook
delivery (ADR-018), in-process rate limiting (ADR-011), and a synchronous, denormalized search
index (ADR-017).

## `webhook_endpoints`

**Drizzle export:** `webhookEndpoints` in `src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts`
**Soft delete:** no — endpoints are deleted outright, not archived
**Tenant column:** `org_id`

| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | TEXT | no (PK) | — | ULID, typed `WebhookId` |
| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | REQ-150, per organization |
| `url` | TEXT | no | — | the receiving endpoint |
| `secret` | TEXT | no | — | signs outgoing payloads, REQ-153 |
| `event_types` | TEXT | no | `'[]'` | JSON array of `TaskflowEventType`; which events this endpoint subscribes to |
| `enabled` | INTEGER (boolean) | no | `true` | REQ-158, disabled endpoints fail fast |
| `created_at` | TEXT | no | now | |
| `updated_at` | TEXT | no | now | |

**Indexes**

| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
|---|---|---|---|
| `webhook_endpoints_org_idx` | `org_id` | no | listing an org's configured endpoints, and the count feeding `PLAN_LIMITS[plan].webhooks` |

**Invariants**

- **Bounded by the plan's webhook quota (REQ-152)** — `countEndpoints` is checked by
  `WebhookService` before `insertEndpoint`, against `PLAN_LIMITS[org.plan].webhooks` (0 for
  free, up to unlimited for enterprise).
- **`secret` is stored in plaintext in this column** — unlike `sessions.token_hash` or
  `invitations.token_hash`, there is no `_hash` suffix on this column and no indication in the
  schema file that it is hashed before storage; it needs to be readable in its original form
  to sign each outgoing delivery's payload (REQ-153), which is a fundamentally different
  requirement from a session or invitation token that only ever needs to be *compared*, never
  reproduced.
- **`event_types` filters which domain events actually enqueue a delivery for this endpoint** —
  an endpoint subscribed to `["issue.created"]` never gets a `webhook_deliveries` row for a
  `comment.created` event; that filtering happens in `WebhookService` before
  `enqueueDelivery` is called, reading this JSON column.

**Read and write paths**

`src/server/repositories/webhook-repository.ts`: `listEndpoints`, `insertEndpoint`,
`updateEndpoint`, `deleteEndpoint`, `countEndpoints`. `WebhookService` is the sole caller for
configuration; endpoint management additionally requires admin (REQ-151), enforced by
`can()`, not by this table.

## `webhook_deliveries`

**Drizzle export:** `webhookDeliveries` in `src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts`
**Soft delete:** no — a delivery's outcome is tracked by `status`, not by archiving
**Tenant column:** `org_id`

| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | TEXT | no (PK) | — | ULID |
| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | denormalized alongside `endpoint_id`, per ADR-006 |
| `endpoint_id` | TEXT | no | — | typed `WebhookId` |
| `event_type` | TEXT | no | — | REQ-160, the event this delivery carries |
| `payload` | TEXT | no | — | REQ-160, the full event envelope, serialized |
| `status` | TEXT | no | `'pending'` | enum: `pending`, `delivered`, `failed` |
| `attempts` | INTEGER | no | `0` | REQ-157's ceiling check, against `WEBHOOK_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5` |
| `last_error` | TEXT | yes | — | most recent failure detail, for REQ-159's visibility in settings |
| `delivered_at` | TEXT | yes | — | null until a successful delivery |
| `created_at` | TEXT | no | now | |
| `updated_at` | TEXT | no | now | bumped on every delivery attempt |

**Indexes**

| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
|---|---|---|---|
| `webhook_deliveries_org_status_idx` | `org_id, status` | no | the dispatcher's claim query — finding `pending` deliveries to attempt next (REQ-154, REQ-155) |

**Invariants**

- **Deliveries are queued, never sent inline with the request that triggered them (REQ-154).**
  `enqueueDelivery` only ever writes a `pending` row; the actual HTTP call happens in a
  separate dispatch pass driven by `claimPendingDeliveries`, which is REQ-155's "claimed in
  bounded batches."
- **Failed deliveries retry with exponential backoff up to a fixed ceiling (REQ-156,
  REQ-157).** `attempts` increments on each try; once it reaches `WEBHOOK_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (5, from
  `src/config/constants.ts`), `markDeliveryFailed` presumably sets a terminal `status: 'failed'`
  rather than allowing further retries — the backoff *timing* itself is not stored as a column
  here (no `next_attempt_at`-style field exists), so the scheduling of *when* the next retry
  happens is computed by the dispatcher at claim time from `attempts` and `updated_at`, not
  read from a persisted "next attempt due" value.
- **Deliveries to a disabled endpoint fail fast (REQ-158)** — `claimPendingDeliveries` or the
  dispatch loop is expected to check `webhook_endpoints.enabled` before attempting a delivery,
  short-circuiting to a failed status without consuming a retry attempt against a genuinely
  unreachable-but-disabled endpoint; this is a cross-table check at dispatch time, not a
  constraint expressed within `webhook_deliveries` itself.

**Read and write paths**

`src/server/repositories/webhook-repository.ts`: `enqueueDelivery`, `claimPendingDeliveries`,
`markDelivered`, `markDeliveryFailed`. Same repository file as `webhook_endpoints`, reflecting
that the two tables are two halves of one feature (configuration and delivery log) rather than
independently owned. `WebhookService` is the sole caller.

## `rate_limit_buckets`

**Drizzle export:** `rateLimitBuckets` in `src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts`
**Soft delete:** no
**Tenant column:** `org_id`

| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | TEXT | no (PK) | — | ULID |
| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | |
| `bucket_key` | TEXT | no | — | identifies which rate-limited operation this bucket tracks |
| `tokens` | INTEGER | no | — | current token count (token-bucket algorithm) |
| `refilled_at` | TEXT | no | — | last refill timestamp |

**Indexes**

| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rate_limit_org_key_idx` | `org_id, bucket_key` | no | the point lookup every rate-limited operation performs before proceeding |

**Invariants**

- **This table is generic infrastructure, shared across every rate-limited feature in the
  product** — the schema file's own comment says it plainly: "Token-bucket state for
  `src/lib/rate-limit.ts`, persisted per org+key." Comment creation (REQ-096), password reset
  (REQ-208), search queries (REQ-176), and webhook delivery (REQ-161) are four independently
  documented requirements that all rate-limit per organization, and this one table backs all
  four rather than each feature declaring its own bucket table — `bucket_key` is what
  distinguishes one feature's bucket from another's for the same org.
- **ADR-011 ("in-process rate limiter") is the design record this table implements.** Being
  backed by a SQLite table rather than an in-memory structure is itself notable: it means rate
  limit state survives a process restart, at the cost of a database round trip on every
  rate-limited operation — a trade-off consistent with this whole application's single-process,
  synchronous, in-process-everything architecture (`better-sqlite3` makes that round trip cheap
  enough to accept).
- No `index` exists on `bucket_key` alone, only the composite `(org_id, bucket_key)` — every
  real query needs both, since rate limiting is always scoped to a specific org.

**Read and write paths**

No dedicated repository file appears under `src/server/repositories/` for this table — unlike
every other table in this dictionary, `rate_limit_buckets` has no `rate-limit-repository.ts`.
Per the schema file's comment, it is read and written directly by `src/lib/rate-limit.ts`,
which sits at the `lib` layer rather than the `repositories` layer — a deliberate placement,
since rate limiting is a cross-cutting concern several different services call into (comment
creation, password reset, search, webhook delivery), not a single domain's owned table the way
every other table in this directory is owned by exactly one repository file.

## `search_index`

**Drizzle export:** `searchIndex` in `src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts`
**Soft delete:** no — entries are deleted on archive (REQ-174), not archived themselves
**Tenant column:** `org_id`

| column | SQL type | null | default | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | TEXT | no (PK) | — | ULID |
| `org_id` | TEXT | no | — | REQ-171, the index is scoped by organization |
| `subject_kind` | TEXT | no | — | enum: `issue`, `comment`, `project` (REQ-170's three covered subject kinds) |
| `subject_id` | TEXT | no | — | the id of the indexed row |
| `project_id` | TEXT | yes | — | denormalized, present for issue/comment subjects, absent (or self-referential) for a project subject; supports project-scoped search filtering |
| `content` | TEXT | no | — | the denormalized, indexable text extracted from the subject |
| `indexed_at` | TEXT | no | — | when this entry was last (re)built |

**Indexes**

| name | columns | unique | why it exists |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search_index_org_kind_idx` | `org_id, subject_kind` | no | scoping a search to specific subject kinds within an org |
| `search_index_org_updated_idx` | `org_id, updated_at` | no | letting the reindex job find the stalest documents first without a full scan |

**Invariants**

- **This is a denormalized, synchronously-maintained index, per ADR-017 ("synchronous search
  index").** The schema file's own comment calls it "maintained by `SearchService`" — every
  write to an issue, comment, or project that affects its indexable content is expected to
  also call `upsertSearchDocument`, synchronously, as part of the same request, rather than
  through an asynchronous background indexer. This is consistent with the whole application's
  single-process, single-writer model (no message queue, no separate search service process).
- **The index is maintained from domain events (REQ-172), and handlers re-read the row rather
  than trusting the event payload (REQ-173)** — `upsertSearchDocument`'s caller is expected to
  fetch the current, authoritative row (from `issues`, `comments`, or `projects`) rather than
  index whatever data happened to be attached to the triggering event, which guards against
  indexing stale or partial data if the event payload and the row's current state have
  diverged by the time the handler runs.
- **Archiving removes a subject from the index (REQ-174)** — `deleteSearchDocument` is called
  when an issue, comment, or project is archived, meaning `search_index` never contains an
  entry for a currently-archived subject; a subsequent restore is expected to
  re-`upsertSearchDocument` it, since a plain "unarchive" alone would not resurrect a deleted
  index row.
- There is no full-text search extension (like SQLite's `FTS5`) declared anywhere in this
  schema or in `drizzle.config.ts` — `content` is a plain `TEXT` column, and `searchDocuments`'s
  matching logic (substring or a similar SQL-`LIKE`-shaped predicate, most likely, though the
  exact matching algorithm is internal to that function rather than expressed by this table's
  columns) is not backed by a dedicated search index structure at the SQLite level, only by the
  `search_index_org_kind_idx` composite index narrowing the row set a query scans.

**Read and write paths**

`src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts`: `upsertSearchDocument`,
`deleteSearchDocument`, `searchDocuments` (keyset-paginated, REQ-179), `countIndexed`.
`SearchService` is the sole caller, and per REQ-180 it also exposes a scheduled full-rebuild
path that presumably clears and re-populates this table from the live `issues`/`comments`/
`projects` tables rather than relying solely on the incremental, event-driven updates staying
perfectly in sync over time.

**Notes**

Grouping `search_index` alongside `webhook_endpoints`/`webhook_deliveries` and
`rate_limit_buckets` in one schema file (and one documentation file) reflects that all four are
supporting infrastructure for the product's core domain rather than domain entities themselves
— none of the four has a corresponding concept a user directly creates and names the way an
issue, project, or comment does. `search_index` is the one table among these four that is
purely derived data: every column's value is computable, in principle, from the `issues`,
`comments`, and `projects` tables plus the extraction logic in `SearchService`, which is why
REQ-180's rebuild capability exists at all — a corrupted or drifted `search_index` can always
be thrown away and regenerated without losing any information that isn't already recoverable
from the tables it was built from.
